title: Review: order revenue mart and export endpoint

scope.goal: Daily revenue per order in `fct_order_revenue`, exported as CSV by `GET /orders/export`

files.what: New mart: one row per order with total revenue, read by dashboard, report and export

findings.summary: join to `order_items` multiplies `order_total` per item · sum item amounts instead
findings.problem: `order_total` is summed after joining `order_items`, so an order with 3 items counts 3 times.
findings.why: Revenue on the dashboard and monthly report is overstated for every multi-item order.
findings.fix: Sum `order_items.amount` (item grain) or join after aggregating items to order grain.
findings.code:
select o.order_id, sum(i.amount) as revenue
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
join {{ ref('stg_order_items') }} i using (order_id)
group by o.order_id

diagram.title: revenue fan-out, one order
diagram.notice: the join copies the order total onto every item row; the sum counts it once per item

files.what: New endpoint `GET /orders/export`: filters the mart by date and streams CSV

findings.summary: `from_date` query param formatted into SQL · use a bound parameter
findings.problem: The `from_date` request value is put into the SQL string with an f-string.
findings.why: Any caller can run arbitrary SQL against the warehouse (SQL injection).
findings.fix: Pass it as a bound parameter.

findings.summary: export has no row limit or date range cap · cap the range to 31 days
findings.problem: A request without `to_date` exports every order since `from_date` in one response.
findings.why: A wide range loads millions of rows into one request and times out.
findings.fix: Require `to_date` and reject ranges over 31 days with a 400.

questions: Should refunds lower revenue in `fct_order_revenue`, or is that a separate mart?

impact.title: fct_order_revenue area
impact.notice: all three readers inherit the fan-out in Must 1

unused: old CSV writer, replaced by the new endpoint
net_size: could drop ~20 of the 142 added lines (duplicate date parsing in the endpoint)

other.what: only the happy path is tested
other.why: the injection and range fixes have no regression test
other.impact: one bad-input test catches both; without it they can return
